text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri will visit Damascus today to discuss regional issues with Syrian officials.
-Brazilian Foreign Minister Lamperia hoped that the U.N. resolution 425, which calls for Israel's withdrawal from south Lebanon, be respected.
-President Clinton assured Lebanon in a letter addressed to President Hrawi that the United States was committed to assisting Lebanon in its development and reconstruction.
-Israeli shelling hits a house in south Lebanon.
-Hizbollah deputy chief Sheikh Qassem said Tuesday's crash of two Israeli helicopters was divine revenge for the children and innocents killed by Israeli shelling in south Lebanon.
-Foreign Minister Bouez said Israel should draw a lesson from the incident and realise it is time to end its occupation of south Lebanon.
-U.S. ambassador to Lebanon Jones expressed his country's satisfaction with the level of Lebanese cooperation in fighting drugs.
-The cabinet demands private schools to freeze any tuition fees increase.
-Public schoolteachers demanded a 20 percent salary increase similar to the one granted last year to private sector employees.
